entry.title: Chile Is Longer Than Lisbon to Moscow
entry.summary: How long is Chile? 4,270 km from north to south, but only 177 km wide on average. Lay it over Europe with its southern tip on Lisbon and it doesn't stop at Moscow: it keeps going for another 360 km, crossing ten countries on the way.

entry.title: Why Is Norway Richer Than Sweden?
entry.summary: Why is Norway so rich? In 1970 Sweden was 44% richer per person. Then the North Sea was split down the middle in 1965, Ekofisk was found on Norway's side in 1969, and Norway taxed the oil and saved it abroad: a fund now worth over $2 trillion.

entry.title: Kaliningrad: Why Does Russia Own It?
entry.summary: Why does Russia own Kaliningrad, a piece of land squeezed between Poland and Lithuania, inside the EU and NATO and two countries away from the rest of Russia? We rewind to 1945, when it was still the German city of Königsberg.

entry.title: Russia Sold Alaska for 2 Cents an Acre
entry.summary: Why did Russia sell Alaska? In 1867 it was hard to defend, far from St Petersburg and next door to British Canada, so Russia sold it to the United States for $7.2 million: about two cents an acre. Today Alaska pumps $7 million worth of oil every few hours.

entry.title: How Much of Ukraine Does Russia Control?
entry.summary: How much of Ukraine does Russia control? About 19% in November 2026, according to DeepStateMap: roughly 114,000 km², an area bigger than Portugal. We rewind the map to 2013 and watch the front line move, month by month.

entry.title: The True Size of Africa: US, India and EU Fit
entry.summary: What is the true size of Africa? On a Mercator map Greenland looks just as big, but Africa is 14 times larger: the mainland US, India and all 27 EU countries fit inside it at the same time, with almost half the continent to spare.

entry.title: Lesotho: The Country Inside South Africa
entry.summary: Why is Lesotho inside South Africa? It's a whole independent country, about the size of Belgium, completely surrounded by a single neighbour. Even its lowest point sits 1,400 metres above sea level: a world record.
